generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The old `VersionCompatibilityChecks` (in `x-pack/plugin/ql`) is deleted and a new one is created in `x-pack/plugin/sql`. The new version correctly uses `SqlVersion` instead of `Version`, and the delegation to `VersionCompatibility` methods is clean. No issues here.

`VersionCompatibility` is declared as `public class` with only static members. It should be `public final class` with a private constructor to prevent instantiation and subclassing, consistent with the style of the old `VersionCompatibilityChecks` (which was `public final class` with `private VersionCompatibilityChecks() {}`) and other utility classes in the codebase (e.g., `StringUtils`, `SqlVersionUtils`).

In `testNoExceptionThrownForCompatibleVersions`, the current version is appended to the list unconditionally:
```java
afterVersionCompatibility.add(VersionTests.current());
```
If `VersionTests.current()` resolves to a version already present in `SqlVersions.getAllVersions()` (e.g., `8.16.0` in a release build), it will appear twice in the list, causing the test to exercise that version redundantly. Consider checking for membership before adding, or using a `LinkedHashSet` to deduplicate.

In `getNextVersion`, the error message is a copy-paste from `getPreviousVersion`:
```java
throw new IllegalArgumentException("couldn't find any released versions before [" + version + "]");
```
This should say "after" since we're looking for the next (higher) version.

Neither `getPreviousVersion` nor `getNextVersion` checks whether `Collections.binarySearch` actually found the element. If the version is not in `DECLARED_VERSIONS`, `binarySearch` returns a negative value (`-(insertionPoint) - 1`). In `getNextVersion`, a negative index that is less than `size - 1` would pass the guard, and `DECLARED_VERSIONS.get(index + 1)` could return an incorrect element or throw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. A check like `if (index < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException(...)` should be added to both methods.

review_comment: Ah, `SqlVersion` doesn't implement `VersionId`. If it implements `VersionId<T>` then this method will come for free
Right, there's no `.before()` method and `SqlVersion` can't implement `VersionId<T>`, since it's in a package very light in dependencies.

This is the `minCompatibleShardNode` - which is still a `Version`. If the version is locked at 8.16, this means this parameter can be completely removed on v9 and replaced with another mechanism if/when SQL needs to be updated?

> this means this parameter can be completely removed on v9

I would think so, assuming that we have an upgrade procedure to 9.x similar to [the existing 7.x to 8.x one](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elastic-stack/current/upgrading-elastic-stack.html#prepare-to-upgrade): upgrade to the latest 8.x one and then the target 9.x. This would mean that the SearchRequest wouldn't need to be given a min (shard) version, since all the nodes in the cluster would respect that condition already.

I think the above would stand independent on SQL being updated or not.
